conviction_note: Sum of three findings (+1.5, -0.8, +1.5) rounded to +2.2: an accelerating primary channel read from Credo's own named AEC contract manufacturer through the quarter just closed, offset by the absence of a pre-announcement that the company has previously used when a quarter blew out, and a positive lean against a +7.31 vol-point put skew whose two known crash triggers (the Q2 revenue guide shape and the gross-margin guide) were both pre-committed by management on 1 June — deliberately well inside the measured 9.6% implied move.

findings.finding: BizLink (3665.TW), named in Credo's FY2026 10-K as the third-party manufacturer of its AEC products, printed accelerating record monthly revenue straight through Credo's fiscal Q1 (3 May - 1 Aug 2026): May NT$7.352bn (-0.4% MoM, +41.3% YoY), June NT$8.518bn (+15.9% MoM, +63.8% YoY), July NT$9.630bn (+13.1% MoM, +59.6% YoY, all-time high) — roughly +31% across the May-to-July span against a Credo revenue guide implying only +6.4% to +8.7% sequential.
findings.why_not_priced: Taiwan-exchange monthly revenue filings are not carried in any US sell-side preview of CRDO — the Zacks, Seeking Alpha and Investing.com previews all frame the quarter off the company's own $465-475m guide and the ~$471.7m consensus with no channel data at all. If the market had made this read, the front-expiry 25-delta skew would not sit at +7.31 vol points to the put side, and the stock would not have surrendered the entire $283-to-$216 August move into a print whose sole named AEC manufacturer was printing back-to-back record months. The BizLink July figure is dated 5 August 2026 (year confirmed in the technews.tw URL path /2026/08/05/), i.e. after Credo last spoke on 1 June and inside the quarter being reported.
findings.independence: Three independent post-1-June datapoints point the same way, none of them Credo's and none sharing a document with each other or with BizLink: Amphenol's Q2 2026 (29 July) IT datacom sales +89% reported / +63% organic with company book-to-bill 1.23:1 (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/APH/amphenol-reports-record-second-quarter-2026-4qu1ti0ylasq.html); Fabrinet's FQ4 2026 (17 August) datacenter revenue $669m, +68% YoY, with FQ1 guided to $1.375-1.425bn (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/17/3346479/0/en/fabrinet-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results.html); and Marvell's FQ2 2027 (27 August) beat with FY27 and FY28 revenue outlooks both raised (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260827816134/en/Marvell-Technology-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2027-Financial-Results). The BizLink-manufactures-Credo's-AECs link is verified in the 10-K itself: 'BizLink Technology, Inc. (BizLink) for manufacturing our AEC products' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001807794/000162828026043303/crdo-20260502.htm).

findings.finding: Credo filed no Item 2.02 8-K — indeed no 8-K of any kind — between 1 June and 1 September 2026, even though this quarter has the same ~31-day quarter-end-to-print gap (ended 1 Aug, prints 1 Sep) as fiscal Q3 2026 (ended 31 Jan, printed 2 Mar), when on 9 February 2026 it pre-announced preliminary revenue of $404-408m against prior guidance of $335-345m nine days after quarter end.
findings.why_not_priced: No aggregator publishes the fact that a company did not file. The EDGAR 8-K list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001807794&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=20) shows the last 8-K as 2026-06-01, so under an identical calendar structure the company chose silence where it once chose to disclose a ~19%-above-guide quarter. That thins the fat right tail. If the market had drawn this inference, front-month ATM IV would not be 140.7% and the three-day straddle would not be pricing an 11.73% move; the option market is still paying for a Feb-9-style shock in either direction.
findings.independence: none — this is an absence-of-filing inference and nothing independently corroborates a negative reading of it. It is deliberately sized small and asymmetric for that reason.

findings.finding: Both mechanisms that could crash this print were pre-committed by management on the 1 June call: the CFO guided Q2 FY27 sequential growth as 'mid single digits, between our Q1 guide, and you can expect something similar in our Q2 guide' (i.e. roughly $490-500m), and guided FY27 non-GAAP gross margin 'to be broadly consistent with fiscal year 2026 levels' — whereas the -14.81% reaction on 2 March 2026 was caused specifically by cutting the Q4 non-GAAP gross-margin guide to 64-66% from 68.6% reported, not by revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews in circulation (Seeking Alpha's '$600M optical revenue ramp in focus', Zacks' 'CRDO Bets on Optical Boom to Drive 80%+ Growth') frame the story as an H2 hockey stick and never state that the Q2 number is already pre-guided to mid-single-digit sequential — so a Q2 guide near $495m, which screens as a violent deceleration off 108-113% YoY growth, carries no new information. If the market had priced that, the 25-delta skew would not be +7.31 vol points put-side on a name whose put/call open interest ratio is only 0.81 and which has already round-tripped -24% from its 18 August level; the skew is paying for a guidance shock whose shape and margin floor were both put on the record three months ago.
findings.independence: Corroborated from a different document that the March crash was a margin event, not a revenue event: the 2 March 2026 print beat on both lines ($407m revenue, $1.07 non-GAAP EPS vs $0.94 consensus) and still fell, with the Q4 non-GAAP GM guide of 64-66% named as the cause (https://www.alphaspread.com/market-news/earnings/credo-posts-strong-q3-fiscal-2026-results-revenue-soars-but-stock-falls). Note this finding shares the 1 June transcript with nothing else in this file, but it and finding 2 are two different readings of the same broad thesis — that the realised move should land inside the 9.6% implied — and should be collapsed if the scorer treats that as one claim.

searched_and_found_nothing: Quiet 8-K between 1 June and 1 September 2026 — there is none; EDGAR shows the last 8-K as the 1 June Q4 release
Executive or CFO departure — Dan Fleming still listed as CFO, no Item 5.02 8-K since 29 October 2025
Form 4 cluster — the only notable recent insider activity is CEO Brennan's 13 July 2026 bona-fide gifts of 300,000 shares between family trusts at $0.00, not open-market sales

Careers page as a headcount signal — 41 open roles across San Jose, Modiin, Ottawa, Pittsburgh, Singapore including a Silicon Photonics team, but no archived snapshot exists to establish a trend, so no finding

Customer-concentration mix change — already disclosed and covered: four customers >10% in Q4 FY26 at 34/27/16/10%, management guiding 3-4 customers >10% going forward, and Zacks has published a diversification piece

Non-cancellable purchase commitments and inventory as a forward indicator — Q1 FY27 10-Q is not filed yet, and the FY26 10-K notes were not retrievable through the fetch layer; inventory at $250.8m vs $90.0m is up 179% against revenue up 157%, which is unremarkable for a doubling business

DustPhotonics dilution or a hidden opex/interest-income step-up — the 1 June call already guided Q1 non-GAAP opex to $86-90m, FY27 opex +~50% YoY, and the $750m net cash outflow in Q1, and consensus $1.17 ties almost exactly to the guide midpoint, so there is no modelling gap
Hyperscaler capex direction — Amazon, Alphabet and Meta all raised 2026 capex in late July 2026 and the ~$760bn aggregate is wall-to-wall CNBC/Statista coverage; fully priced

The 31 August 2026 Toucan PCIe 6.x compliance listing and Open CPX MSA membership, and the 10 August OmniConnect OCP contribution — real, dated, but standards/roadmap items already in trade press (StockTitan, Converge Digest, HPCwire) with no bearing on the quarter
Taiwan supply-chain press (DigiTimes-style) reports of AEC order cuts, share loss or a second source at any hyperscaler — nothing found

Evidence that a hyperscaler is insourcing AECs or designing copper out of next-gen racks — no dated primary source found; Marvell's 27 August call talked up CPO/NPO and 'end-to-end portfolio' but said nothing about AECs
baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline: the +7.31 vol-point put skew and the 24% give-back from the 18 August high say the market is paying for a downside shock, while the only primary channel data inside the quarter is accelerating and the two triggers that have historically produced this stock's crashes were both pre-committed by management on 1 June — though the absence of a pre-announcement, which the baseline cannot see, argues the upside tail is thinner than 140.7% IV implies.
